summary: Livingstone Fire Lookout on Thrift Peak: a 1956 wood-frame original, a July 1975 foundation for a new lookout, a June 2009 observer visit, and no source on access today.

facts.design: Original lookout building (1956) was a 12 x 12 wood frame structure

access.note: No source read says whether the lookout building is open to visitors. The peak is reached by a moderate one-way trail in Bob Creek Wildland Provincial Park.

visit.trail_note: The usual route requires fording the Oldman River and hiking several kilometres up a road (2009 trip report)

events.note: Original 12 x 12 wood frame lookout structure
Foundation laid in July 1975 for a new lookout a few yards away, per a Calgary Herald report quoted by the archive
Lookout observer met a June 2009 visiting group on the helipad

evidence.supports: Livingstone Fire Lookout tops Thrift Peak; the lookout log calls it rarely visited
evidence.quote: According to the lookout log, Livingstone Fire Lookout, which tops Thrift Peak, is rarely visited.

evidence.supports: site is in the Oldman River area
trail to Thrift Peak is moderate, one way, in Bob Creek Wildland Provincial Park
evidence.quote: This is a moderate one way trail to Thrift Peak in Bob Creek Wildland Provincial Park.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Bob Spirko and the trail listing use Livingstone; the archive heading reads Livingston Ridge. The story uses Livingstone for the lookout and the archive's wording where it quotes the archive.

sources.title: Thrift Peak via Livingstone Fire Lookout Trail

notes_for_editor: Brief record says access closed, staffed March to October, height 2.0 m and kind ground. None of these appears in a source read, so height is left out of facts. Access is set to restricted because no source states a closure; a human should check the closed status. The April to October staffing line is Alberta-wide, not Livingstone-specific. The 2009 visit is the last first-hand account; the trail listings are undated. Searches used: 2. Page reads: about 6. Agency is the brief's Alberta Wildfire, supported only by the Alberta-wide statement.
